paragraphs.text: A robot can weld a car in seconds but takes minutes to fold a towel. Cloth changes shape as it is touched, so the machine cannot predict what it will be holding next.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: One laboratory solved part of the problem by giving the robot two cheap cameras and letting it shake each item first, which drops the cloth into a small number of predictable shapes.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Laundries are watching. A machine that folds hotel sheets already exists, but the items must be fed in flat, and a human still does that part of the work.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Researchers say the real prize is elsewhere. Handling soft, changing material would help in harvesting fruit and in surgery, where tissue behaves much like cloth.
paragraphs.label: D

items.prompt: an explanation of why the task is difficult for machines
a trick that made the problem simpler
a use of the research outside the home
a limit of a machine that is already in use

groups.instruction: Questions 1–4. Which paragraph contains the following information? Write the correct letter, A–D. NB You may use any letter more than once.
